newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money slumps to close at 1.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money slumps to close at 1.0 percent.

text.p: Indian call money slumped to close at 0.50-1.50 percent on Wednesday, compared to the day's opening quotes of 3.50-4.50, dealers said.
"The lacklustre demand and the squared positions with banks resulted in call rates crashing to 1.0 percent," a dealer said.
But most of day's deals were in the region of 3.00-3.25 percent, they said.
"Thursday will see some demand for funds from bankers who have covered only 85 percent of their total reserves," one dealer said. "The call rates will open at 3.0 percent on Thursday," he said.
The market saw a repo transaction for 500 million rupees in the secondary market for three days at 4.00 percent, a primary dealer said.

"A correction in security prices have taken place and the yields have been aligned," Mithi Somesh, a dealer at Lloyds Brokerage said. "Last few days saw security prices falling, despite of the easy call levels," Mithi said.

The 13.25 percent 1997 stock rose by 10 basis points to 101.05, zero coupon bond maturing in 1999 rose by 13 basis points to 77.85 rupees, while 13.50 percent 1997 stock rose by 15 basis points to 102.50 rupees, dealers said.
The yields on treasury bills also fell marginally.
The August 1997 maturity treasury bills fell to 9.90 percent from its previous yield of 10.0 percent, while September maturity treasury bills yield was unchanged at 10.0 percent.
There were no deals in certificates of deposit and commercial paper, dealers said.
